members.note: Writes FDreamListStyle::RowHeight and switches StyleSource to Inline, so the next style push does not throw the number away.
Writes FDreamTileViewStyle::TileWidth. A different width is a different column count, so it re-flows rather than repaints.
Off the RESOLVED style, so a tile view wearing the project sheet answers with the size it is actually drawn at.
Off the resolved style, as GetEntryHeight is.
The SAME field a list's row height comes from, because it is the same measurement. One tile, one size, and the style holds it -- a second field on the control would be the same number written twice.
The one thing a tile adds to a row. No aspect lock and no square flag: two numbers already say every shape those would, and a lock makes one of the two unreadable in the panel.

EDreamTileAlignment, UMG's seven answers. LeftAligned by default, not UMG's EvenlyDistributed: it is what every tile view here has drawn, and a grid that re-spaced itself on upgrade would be a layout change nobody asked for. All seven are one function, ResolveLineLayout, which returns the line's start, its tile size and its pitch TOGETHER -- they are three views of the same leftover space, and answering them separately is how two modes end up disagreeing about it. EvenlySize sizes by the COLUMN count so every line matches; Fill sizes by THIS line's count so a short last line stretches. That is the only difference between them.

Answered by INDEX in UDreamTileView::GetNavigationTarget, not by geometry: off the end of a line is the first tile of the next, and the tile it lands on is at the OPPOSITE edge of the control -- exactly the step a nearest-rect navigator cannot make. GetNavigationTarget is what a navigation press on a tile steps by, so the switch reaches the player. Off by default, as UMG's is: a press off the end of a line then leaves the tile view.
AutoHide already means 'gone while everything fits', which is the state UMG's disabled visibility describes. A second enum for the disabled case would be a second answer.

A switch over whether the authored size is the tile or the tile plus its gap. Here they are two fields that are never added into one: TileWidth is the tile and TileSpacing is the gap beside it, so there is no ambiguity for a flag to resolve.
